title: AHB Core and Version-Specific Signal Reference
description: Expand a signal to check its source, phase, values, revision scope, and the verification mistake most likely to corrupt a transaction model.

signals.name: HCLK
signals.description: All AHB transfer timing is related to the rising edge of HCLK.
signals.verificationNote: Sample protocol state on the specified edge; a sub-cycle combinational transition is not a second transfer.

signals.name: HRESETn
signals.description: Resets the bus and participating components. Assertion can be asynchronous; deassertion is synchronized to HCLK.
signals.verificationNote: Test reset during traffic and verify a safe first address phase after release.

signals.name: HADDR
signals.description: Identifies the byte address for the current address phase.
signals.sampled: With HREADY HIGH for a valid NONSEQ/SEQ transfer
signals.verificationNote: Queue accepted addresses; do not associate current HADDR directly with current HRDATA/HRESP.

signals.name: HTRANS
signals.description: Classifies the current address phase as IDLE, BUSY, NONSEQ, or SEQ.
signals.verificationNote: Track burst context: INCR may terminate after BUSY, while a fixed burst must finish on SEQ.

signals.name: HWRITE
signals.description: Selects write when HIGH and read when LOW for the address phase.
signals.verificationNote: Delay direction with the accepted address when determining which later data bus owns the transfer.

signals.name: HSIZE
signals.description: Encodes the number of bytes transferred by one beat.
signals.verificationNote: Check natural alignment, active byte lanes, and address increment of 2^HSIZE.

signals.name: HBURST
signals.description: Defines SINGLE, undefined INCR, and fixed incrementing or wrapping burst forms.
signals.sampled: First and continuing accepted address phases
signals.verificationNote: Cross with HSIZE and verify count, wrap span, early termination rules, and the 1 KB boundary.

signals.name: HPROT[3:0]
signals.description: Carries data/instruction, privileged, bufferable, and cacheable/modifiable information according to the implemented revision.
signals.verificationNote: Treat attributes as part of transaction identity and keep them stable with the pending valid transfer.

signals.name: HMASTLOCK
signals.description: Indicates that the current transfer is part of a locked sequence. Original shared AHB derives the bus-level value through the arbiter; AHB-Lite/AHB5 include it on the interface.
signals.verificationNote: Do not confuse locked ownership with HEXCL or security state.

signals.name: HWDATA
signals.description: Carries write data in the data phase following its accepted write address phase.
signals.sampled: When the write data phase completes with HREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Hold stalled write data stable and associate it with the previous accepted address, not current HADDR.

signals.name: HRDATA
signals.description: Carries read data from the selected slave through the return-data mux.
signals.sampled: Read data-phase completion with HREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Only compare data on completion and attribute it to the queued read address.

signals.name: HRESP
signals.description: Reports completion status. AHB-Lite/AHB5 use one-bit OKAY/ERROR; original AHB uses a wider encoding that also includes RETRY/SPLIT.
signals.direction: Selected slave through response mux → master
signals.verificationNote: Select response rules by interface revision and recognize both cycles of ERROR.

signals.name: HREADYOUT
signals.description: An individual slave indicates whether its current data phase is pending or complete.
signals.verificationNote: Review system muxing and timing to prevent a combinational loop through the selected HREADY path.

signals.name: HREADY
signals.description: The return mux presents the selected slave's completion state to the master and all slaves so address and data phases advance together.
signals.verificationNote: A monitor advances its accepted-phase queues only when HREADY is HIGH.

signals.name: HSELx
signals.description: A combinational decode of high-order HADDR selects one target for the address phase.
signals.sampled: By the slave only with HREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Do not asynchronously consume transient HSEL changes as accepted transfers.

signals.name: HBUSREQx
signals.description: A master requests ownership of the original shared AHB bus.
signals.verificationNote: A request does not equal ownership; combine the selected HGRANTx with HREADY at the accepting edge.

signals.name: HGRANTx
signals.description: The arbiter identifies the highest-priority eligible requester for next ownership.
signals.verificationNote: Keep current HMASTER unchanged through a stalled handover.

signals.name: HLOCKx
signals.description: A requesting master tells the arbiter that its upcoming sequence must be indivisible.
signals.sampled: With HBUSREQx before the locked address phase
signals.verificationNote: Distinguish this request from the arbiter's aligned bus-level HMASTLOCK output.

signals.name: HMASTER
signals.description: Original AHB uses arbiter-generated HMASTER for shared-bus identity. AHB5 uses an implementation-defined-width identity when Exclusive_Transfers is supported and can extend it in the interconnect.
signals.verificationNote: Do not assume the same source or width across revisions.

signals.name: HSPLITx
signals.description: A SPLIT-capable slave tells the original AHB arbiter which master may reattempt a split transfer.
signals.verificationNote: This signal and SPLIT/RETRY behavior do not exist on AHB-Lite/AHB5 interfaces.

signals.name: HNONSEC
signals.description: Present when Secure_Transfers is declared; labels the address phase Secure or Non-secure.
signals.verificationNote: Verify explicit adaptation at boundaries where one interface lacks the capability.

signals.name: HEXCL
signals.description: Present when Exclusive_Transfers is declared; marks a NONSEQ transfer as part of an exclusive sequence.
signals.verificationNote: Exclusive transfers are single-transfer SINGLE/INCR forms, contain no BUSY, and must be aligned.

signals.name: HEXOKAY
signals.description: Reports success or failure of an exclusive transfer; for a write, success means memory was updated.
signals.verificationNote: HEXOKAY must not be asserted with HRESP=ERROR, and HEXOKAY=0 is not itself an ERROR.

signals.name: HPROT[6:4]
signals.description: Present when Extended_Memory_Types is declared; extends the base protection attributes with lookup, allocation, and shareability information.
signals.verificationNote: Gate checkers by the declared property and verify legacy HPROT adaptation explicitly.
